entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Waleran III of Luxembourg Count of Ligny and Saint Pol was a French nobleman and soldier.

Born into the Luxembourg duchy in the late 14th century, Waleran III rose to prominence through his military prowess and strategic alliances. As a key figure in the Burgundian-Valois conflict, he played a crucial role in the complex web of power struggles that shaped Western Europe during the Late Middle Ages.

His military campaigns, including the Battle of Agincourt in 1415, cemented his reputation as a skilled commander. However, his legacy is also marked by controversy, as he was accused of treason and eventually executed for his alleged involvement in the murder of his cousin, John the Fearless, Duke of Burgundy.

Waleran III's life and actions serve as a testament to the intricate politics and military tactics of the era, highlighting the complexities of loyalty, duty, and power in the treacherous world of medieval nobility.

The legacy of Waleran III can be seen in the subsequent conflicts that ravaged Western Europe, including the Hundred Years' War and the rise of the Habsburgs.

In the annals of history, Waleran III's name stands as a reminder of the brutal realities of medieval politics and the devastating consequences of treachery and betrayal.

His story is one of intrigue, power, and the enduring legacy of a bygone era.
